title: NSW anti-protest law ruled unconstitutional after Palestine Action Group court challenge
summary: PAG had challenged expanded police powers to restrict protests near places of worship The New South Wales supreme court has struck down a law that had given police expanded powers to prevent protests near places of worship. title: Brown University rejects Trump proposal to overhaul policies for preferential funding
summary: Brown joins MIT in refusing offer, saying that proposal would ‘restrict academic freedom’ Brown University has become the second higher education institution to turn down an invitation from Donald Trump to sign onto his administration’s controversial 10-page college compact that would overhaul university policies in return for preferential access to federal funding. The “Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education” is a proposed agreement that would impose restrictions on diversity, equity and inclusion programs and limits on international student enrollment. title: PayPal's blockchain partner accidentally minted $300 trillion in stablecoins
summary: In an embarrassing error, PayPal blockchain partner Paxos accidentally minted 300 trillion of the PYUSD token today. PayPal's stablecoin, which it debuted in 2023 , is supposed to be redeemable at a 1:1 rate for US dollars. $300 trillion is more than double the entire world's current GDP of $117 trillion. In short, that's a really bad mistake from Paxos. At least the action did appear to be a mistake. Paxos acknowledged the issue in a post on X, assuring clients that their funds are secure and stating that it burned the excess reserves of stablecoins. The company claimed that "this was an internal technical error.” Maybe so, but internal technical errors can still wreak havoc pretty quickly when it comes to finance, especially in the fantasy worlds of blockchain and crypto. Thanks to the appropriately named Web3 is Going Just Great for picking up on this story.
